correctness.rationale: Every multiple N < \(2^{3m}\) corresponds to three m-bit blocks. Modulo Q=\(2^m-1\), their sum is 0,Q,2Q or 3Q. Excluding N=0, pairing sums Q and 2Q by complement, and treating the all-one 3Q singleton yields the exact enumerator. For sum Q, a 2-state carry automaton has exact transitions with weights (3z,z^3,1,3z^2). Carry excursions exhaust and sharply bound all weights m,...,2m-1; complemented weights and singleton yield the total support m,...,2m,3m. Boundary coefficients follow counting 0/one full or length-2 excursion; recurrence is Cayley-Hamilton. Two-block obstruction proves the first \(m+1\)-weight multiplier is \(2^m+3\). Reproducible exact direct enumeration agrees with transfer computation for 8 exponents, 87898 positive multiples; this finite corroboration is not used as proof of arbitrary m.

originality.rationale: The new claim uniformly and exactly enumerates every binary weight of every positive multiple of \(2^m-1\) below \(2^{3m}\), with explicit gap and boundary counts. Full-text comparisons with Elsholtz 2016 and Clokie et al. 2020 identify only global least-weight / unrestricted attainment and algorithmic results, which do not imply a uniformly parameterized exact three-block polynomial or first next-weight multiplier. Actual broad and alias searches in published-result records yielded unrelated nearby binary-code, sparse-digit, and Mersenne-arithmetic findings, none whose statements imply this finite-window histogram. The old Stolarsky paper was not accessible in full, an explicit residual risk rather than a false no-overlap certification.
residual_risks: Stolarsky 1980 full text inaccessible, so a historically phrased three-block count not entirely excluded.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a complete natural length-constrained digit-sparsity spectrum, the nontrivial terminal gap, and quantitative rarity/first appearance of next-to-minimum Hamming weight for the classic Mersenne multiple problem, uniformly for all \(m\ge2\). A fixed two-state polynomial recurrence replaces nonuniform computations and exposes structural carry geometry. It extends established minimum-weight statements by answering a different meaningful exact counting and finite-cutoff question.
